quarterly_data.quarter: Supermicro press release: Supermicro Now Shipping NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Racks (09-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Supermicro says it is now shipping NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 racks integrated with its Data Center Building Block Solutions (DCBBS) and its direct liquid cooling stack (DLC-2). Each rack holds 72 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs and 36 NVIDIA Vera CPUs: eighteen 1U compute trays, each with four Rubin GPUs and two Vera CPUs, connected through nine sixth-generation NVIDIA NVLink switch trays delivering 216 TB/s of scale-up bandwidth; each rack provides 20.7 TB of HBM4 memory and up to 54 TB of LPDDR5X. The DCBBS Blueprint for one Vera Rubin NVL72 Scalable Unit provides 1,152 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs with 331 TB of HBM4 memory across 16 compute racks, with cooling, power delivery, storage and networking. CEO Charles Liang: customers can now order a Scalable Unit and receive production-ready systems with end-to-end integration (he calls it the most complete solution for the Vera Rubin platform, a company claim). No customers, volumes or dollar figures are stated.
quarterly_data.figure: now shipping Vera Rubin NVL72 racks; per rack 72 Rubin GPUs + 36 Vera CPUs, 20.7 TB of HBM4; per Scalable Unit 1,152 GPUs and 331 TB of HBM4 across 16 compute racks

quarterly_data.quarter: Supermicro press release: Supermicro Now Shipping NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Racks (09-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: For the Vera Rubin NVL72 racks it is now shipping, Supermicro supplies a full liquid-cooling stack (DLC-2) from its own in-house portfolio: cold plates, manifolds, hose kits, rack power shelves, in-row CDUs, in-rack CDUs, Liquid-to-Air sidecar CDUs, rear door heat exchangers and facility-side cooling towers. The in-row cooling distribution units are rated at 1.8MW per CDU and deployed with N+1 redundancy; rear door heat exchangers are optional to capture residual heat. Supermicro says it tests and validates every rack with the full liquid cooling stack before deployment.
quarterly_data.figure: in-row CDU rated at 1.8MW per CDU, N+1 redundancy
